summary:
PARALLAX is an interactive SPHEREx sky exploration platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge.

The project allows users to enter celestial coordinates, select a field of view and detector, and retrieve time-ordered infrared observations from NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA). Its Python backend uses Astropy, NumPy, and Reproject to process FITS images, align observations onto a common sky coordinate grid, and generate image previews. The React and TypeScript frontend provides an interactive observatory with time-lapse playback, image comparison, coordinate controls, and observation notes.

PARALLAX helps users explore how infrared observations of the same region change across different observation dates. It provides a practical way to investigate astronomical targets, inspect real SPHEREx data, and identify potential changes that deserve further scientific analysis.

The project is important because it makes complex astronomical data more accessible and supports public exploration of NASA's SPHEREx observations without claiming unverified discoveries.
details:
PARALLAX is an interactive astronomical exploration platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge.

WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

PARALLAX allows users to explore time-ordered infrared observations of selected regions of the sky using real SPHEREx archive data. Users enter Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) coordinates, select a field of view between 1 and 30 arcminutes, and choose one of six detectors (D1–D6).

The Python backend queries NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) through its Simple Image Access (SIA2) service. It retrieves FITS observations, reads their astronomical metadata, processes image data, masks invalid pixels, and aligns multiple observations onto a common World Coordinate System (WCS) grid. It then generates image previews for the frontend.

The interactive interface displays observations in chronological order. Users can play time-lapse sequences, move between observations, adjust brightness, zoom, pan, inspect coordinates, and record observation notes. It also provides example targets, including Barnard's Star, Epsilon Indi B, WISE 0855, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

SPHEREx produces large volumes of infrared astronomical data. PARALLAX provides an accessible way to explore these observations without requiring users to manually download and process FITS files.

The project supports astronomy education, public engagement with NASA data, and preliminary investigation of changes between observations. It encourages users to examine real astronomical measurements and distinguish observed information from illustrative simulations.

CREATIVITY AND INNOVATION

The main creative element is the combination of real astronomical archive retrieval, scientific image processing, and interactive time-based visualization in one application.

Instead of presenting isolated astronomical images, PARALLAX aligns observations onto a shared sky grid and organizes them chronologically. It also provides coordinate-based exploration, detector selection, observation metadata, and a clearly labeled tutorial mode. The application does not fabricate missing scientific observations or present tutorial imagery as real data.

TECHNOLOGIES AND TOOLS

Frontend:

  • React 19
  • TypeScript
  • Vite
  • HTML and CSS
  • Lucide React

Backend:

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • Uvicorn
  • Astropy
  • NumPy
  • Reproject
  • Requests
  • Pillow

Astronomical data and scientific resources:

  • NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA)
  • SPHEREx DR1 and QR3 data collections
  • FITS image files
  • World Coordinate System (WCS)
  • SIA2 astronomical data access

Testing and development:

  • Playwright
  • Pytest
  • Chromium
  • Git and GitHub

The project runs as a web application and does not require specialized astronomical hardware.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

During development, we considered scientific accuracy, image alignment, observation dates, detector selection, data quality flags, wavelength compatibility, processing limitations, and accessibility.

We also considered unreliable archive connections, large FITS downloads, processing time, memory usage, and the need to communicate errors clearly. The application uses caching, request limits, and explicit archive error messages.

VALIDATION AND SCIENTIFIC LIMITATIONS

The production frontend build passed TypeScript checking and Vite compilation. Backend regression tests and browser workflows passed. Real SPHEREx archive retrieval and image processing were also demonstrated for selected observations.

PARALLAX is an exploration and visualization prototype. It does not claim to have discovered Planet X, measured confirmed planetary motion, or established astronomical variability. Further scientific validation, calibration, and analysis are required before drawing such conclusions.
